text: Placed beside the earlier promise, the difference grows less. Isaac is the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the writer, having reminded us of this, turns that very promise into a test. All depends upon a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times, to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. Its meaning alters. Each time he speaks it, the word means something different and costs him more; and it costs him most when he speaks it the third time, to the angel.
